coaching.headline: No allied deaths in the last two fights, and the team cashed both fights into two inner towers, Orb Prime, two inhibitors and the Core.

flags.text: Lt. Belica was a fucking wrecking ball: ten kills, one death, five of the last nine kills.
Aurora beat Shinbi on the offlane: four of Shinbi's seven deaths, one Aurora death all game.
Serath's 30885 objective damage led all ten players, more than double Wukong's 14868.
Riktor's ten deaths were a shit pattern: six to Skylar, four outside any detected fight.

focus.title: Starve Skylar, cash every won fight
focus.action: After a won fight, take the nearest tower or objective before resetting; when Skylar is unseen, no ally walks the duo lane or enemy jungle without a ward or a partner.

13.5.call: Lost 0-3 in the allied half near mid: Serath fell first to Wukong, then Lt. Belica and Riktor, and the enemy took Fangtooth. With Wukong unseen, concede Fangtooth rather than three bodies.

32.4.call: Won 3-0 after taking Genesis Core: Aurora on Shinbi, Lt. Belica on Steel and Neon, the enemy offlane inner falling between kills. Contest every Genesis Core the same way.

35.1.call: Won 3-0 just after the allied duo outer fell; two inhibitors fell between the Neon and Shinbi kills, and the Core followed the Wukong kill. With two inhibitors down, finish the Core before answering an outer tower.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Output far over the norm: 1064 hero damage per minute against 731, and 11.6 CS per minute against 8. When mid is ahead again, keep farming at the same rate.
Credited with the mid inhibitor, and a rotation kill on Wukong on the enemy offlane came before the allied Fangtooth. When mid is shoved, roam toward the next objective.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Gold finished 19091 to 13108 over Shinbi. After a Shinbi kill outside a fight, walk a wave into the enemy offlane outer while Shinbi is dead.
The only death came to Skylar in the mid fight lost 2-3, then the allied offlane outer fell. Before leaving the offlane for mid, shove the wave first.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Double kill on Shinbi and Wukong on the allied offlane, but the enemy still took Mini Prime. After a jungle double kill, call Prime or a tower.
One ward placed against a 7.4 norm, three destroyed. If wards were equipped but unused, switch to sentry and sweep before ganks and objectives.
Killed Steel on the mid lane outside any detected fight, then took the enemy mid outer seconds later. Against a three-magical comp, add a magic resist item.
a8651833-8f67-456f-9791-22059f96110c: Killed Neon in the enemy jungle, then Skylar on mid seven seconds after Riktor fell there, the only Skylar death. Turn on Skylar whenever Skylar scores.
Hero damage ran 533 per minute against an 831 norm despite 9.8 CS per minute. When Riktor lands Riplash or Skewer, unload on that target.
4e02ae68-47b4-4e3d-a4ea-d69e3e975b17: Ran the vision: 28 wards, the game's most, plus the game's most damage mitigated at 68429. When the duo lane is behind again, hold the same ward pace.
A duo-lane death outside any detected fight came inside a minute before the enemy Mini Prime. When Mini Prime is near, ward the allied duo lane before walking up.
Landed the last kill of the game, Wukong in the enemy base, right before the Core fell. When the enemy base opens, keep joining the final fight.

matchup: Wukong was the jungle opponent: 2/7/4, with Serath ahead on gold, 17326 to 15750.
Wukong's Tainted Trident cuts healing on physical damage, trimming Draconum's takedown restore and Sky Splitter lifesteal.
Skylar took two of three Serath deaths, both in the enemy half.
build: Sky Splitter and Spectra are two of three winning-core items; Tainted Rounds is missing.
Sky Splitter's Rend deals a share of current health on basic attacks; Chastise and Heaven's Fury apply on-hit effects.
Cursed Ring, finished last, raises total attack speed and cuts basic attack damage; earlier fights ran without Cursed Ring.
eternal: Nihil's Doom stacks stats while damaging heroes; Growing Threat adds permanent bonus damage and omnivamp later in the game.
Weald is clearly the field's best Serath jungle Eternal; Nihil has too few games to lead.
Growing Threat with Terror is the best Nihil pair; the Adaptive Plating pair trails.
augment: Crushing Descent adds a brief stun when Ascend deals damage.
Crushing Descent leans ahead of Vital Resonance in the Serath jungle field. Sound keep.
crest: Eviscerator's active grants attack speed, omnivamp and empowered on-hit basic attacks for a short window.
Liberator leans ahead of Pacifier and Eviscerator in the Serath jungle field, on the same Sharpshooter Crest path.
improvement: Weald for Nihil is the field-backed swap: true-damage missiles on low-health heroes, giving up Doom's stat growth.
Liberator for Eviscerator is the crest lean: a cleanse and shield, giving up the attack-speed and omnivamp window.

matchup: Duo was Legion and Riktor against Skylar and Steel; three allied duo deaths before minute ten, zero enemy.
Skylar's 39419 hero damage led all ten players, with two of three Legion deaths.
Steel's Tainted Guard cuts healing for heroes basic-attacking Steel, trimming Terminus lifesteal and the Terminus overheal shield.
build: Vanquisher is the only winning-core item built; Malady and The Perforator are missing.
Demolisher's armor ignore suits a Steel carrying Tainted Guard and Vainglory armor.
Tainted Rounds, finished last, cuts the target's healing on basic attacks; earlier fights against Steel's healing ran without Tainted Rounds.
eternal: Thraex marks the last hero hit by a basic attack: more damage dealt to the mark, less taken.
Savage Strikes with Rallying Roar is the best Thraex pair; Knell leans first, and Thraex trails four Eternals with enough games.
augment: Press the Advantage spawns a Rally Point on takedowns, boosting rate of fire and ally attack speed, without the heal.
Heavy Caliber leans ahead of Scorched Earth in the Legion carry field; Press the Advantage ranks third.
crest: Pacifier's active dashes and empowers the next physical hit, much stronger on low-health targets, with a recast on kills.
Epoch is clearly the field's best Legion carry crest; Pacifier ranks well behind.
improvement: Epoch for Pacifier is the field-backed crest swap: Stasis on demand, giving up the dash and low-health burst.
Epoch builds from Wizard Crest, Pacifier from Sharpshooter Crest, so the swap starts at the first crest buy.
Malady or The Perforator over Nuclear Rounds completes more of the winning core.

matchup: Shinbi was the lane opponent: 0/7/2, yet still dealt 25544 hero damage across the game.
Shinbi and Neon both built Tainted Scepter: magical damage cuts the target's healing.
Circle Rhythm gives Shinbi shields, the target Astral Catalyst's Event Horizon hits for bonus damage.
build: Magnify and Flux Matrix are two of three winning-core items; Elafrost is missing.
Flux Matrix raises magical damage taken by nearby enemy heroes and lowers enemy tenacity, lengthening Hoarfrost roots and Cryoseism stuns.
Astral Catalyst, finished last, hits shielded targets harder; earlier fights ran without Astral Catalyst.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size; Voracity and Feeding Frenzy is the best Krix pair on Aurora offlane.
Krix ranks last among Aurora offlane Eternals with enough games; Knell and Idrisil lead a toss-up.
augment: Hypothermia makes Boreal Sweep hits on heroes shred physical and magical armor and slow attack speed.
Frozen Fury, Hypothermia and Glacial Thorns are a field toss-up on Aurora offlane. Sound keep.
crest: Typhoon stacks attack speed on basic attack hits and dashes at full stacks.
Typhoon leans ahead of Winter's Fury in the Aurora offlane field. Sound keep.
improvement: Knell or Idrisil for Krix are the field-backed Eternal options: armor shred or bonus armor, giving up Krix's health.
Elafrost for Fire Blossom completes the winning core, trading the burn aura for a slowing empowered attack after casts.

matchup: Neon was the lane opponent: three of four Neon deaths went to Lt. Belica, with 22682 gold against 16180.
Neon's Data Burst slows and, overclocked, mesmerises; Erase Vector dashes and slows on the next Jolt.
build: Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings are the full winning core.
Noxia's Dark Matter needs two different abilities on one hero: the first marks, the second deals max-health damage.
Amulet Of Chaos, finished last, cuts basic ability cooldowns on takedowns; earlier fights ran without Amulet Of Chaos.
eternal: Aion stacks mana regeneration on casts and pays gold from spell damage to heroes; Runic Focus turns mana into magical power.
Lotus leans first in the Lt. Belica mid field, Xyris second, Aion third; the minors match the best Aion pair.
augment: Combat Veteran adds movement speed and passive experience every second.
Combat Veteran clearly leads the Lt. Belica mid augment field. Sound keep.
crest: Soulbearer's active gives a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed for a short window.
Typhoon leans first in the Lt. Belica mid crest field, Epoch second, Soulbearer behind both.
improvement: Lotus for Aion is the field lean: random stat gains over time and on takedowns, giving up spell-damage gold.
Typhoon for Soulbearer swaps the shield and lifesteal for attack-speed stacks and a dash; Typhoon starts from Warlock Crest.

matchup: Duo matchup was Skylar and Steel: Skylar took six of ten Riktor deaths, Steel three, two in the enemy jungle.
Steel's Bull Rush and Shield Bash stun, and Shield Slam knocks up and stuns.
Skylar's Atomiser adds missing-health damage, punishing any low-health catch.
build: Xenia and Frosted Lure are two of three winning-core items; Dynamo is missing.
Xenia shields nearby allied heroes; Raiment of Renewal regenerates missing health while out of combat.
Frosted Lure, finished last, slows and shields after time near enemy heroes; earlier fights ran without Frosted Lure.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size; Regenerative Tissue heals after a stretch without hero damage.
Knell leans first in the Riktor support field; Krix trails, and Regenerative Tissue with Cannibalism is the best Krix pair.
augment: Wanton Warden regenerates health from a share of damage taken.
Warden's Leash and Zap O' 9-Chains lead a toss-up in the Riktor support field; Wanton Warden ranks third.
crest: Leafsong's active speeds nearby allies, grants slow immunity and passing through heroes; the Visionary passive raises the ward cap.
Rift Walkers and Saphir's Mantle lead a toss-up in the Riktor support field; Leafsong trails both.
improvement: Rift Walkers for Leafsong stays on the Warden Crest path: a dash and hero pull instead of the team speed burst.
Cannibalism for Feeding Frenzy matches the best Krix pair: permanent health on takedowns over attack speed near enemies.

threats: Heal-stacking: Steel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s), Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Riktor) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
ourKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
ourKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
ourKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

ourKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
ourKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
ourKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
ourKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Riplash pull → Shock Therapy silence → Skewer suppress ult
ourKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
ourKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
ourKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

enemyKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
enemyKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
enemyKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
enemyKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Rushing Beat dashes → Line Tempo wolves → Circle Rhythm shield → All-Kill! wolfpack ult
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Track and unleash All-Kill! in a grouped fight
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread vs the wolfpack; she's squishy without her shield up

enemyKits.combo: Windsurge engage → Cyclebreaker damage-reduction spin → clones from 84000 Hairs
enemyKits.winCondition: stance-dance for damage or tankiness and overwhelm with clones
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights alongside his clones
enemyKits.playAgainst: AoE clears his clones; CC him during the damage-reduction window

enemyKits.combo: Plasma Grenade → Hypercharge on-hit → Air Assault reposition → Atomiser ult
enemyKits.winCondition: Hypercharge and kite-shoot from Air Assault safety
enemyKits.passive: extra jump; kills cause corpse explosions
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline so she can free-fire airborne
enemyKits.playAgainst: CC her out of Air Assault; she's squishy on the ground
